description: Delta is Athens' most ambitious contemporary tasting-menu restaurant, set inside the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center. The cooking is avant-garde, technical and deeply tied to Greek ingredients, with preservation, fermentation and sustainability shaping the experience. Its dramatic dining room and views toward the coast make it a true destination for affluent international diners.
highlights: Greece's only current two-star Michelin restaurant, futuristic SNFCC setting, fermentation-led tasting menu and strong sustainability credentials.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; This is Athens; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Spondi is Athens' grand old fine-dining address, pairing French-influenced haute cuisine with formal service and a deep cellar. Its Pangrati townhouse, garden and discreet salons still feel like the city's classic special-occasion setting. For diners who value polish, longevity and gastronomic pedigree, it remains indispensable.
highlights: Long-running Michelin-starred Athens landmark with French haute cuisine, formal service and a serious wine cellar.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Eater; This is Athens; Official website

description: Soil gives Athens a softer, garden-driven style of fine dining, built around seasonal produce and an intimate Pangrati house. The restaurant feels contemporary and personal rather than showy, with a tasting menu that keeps Greek ingredients at the center. Its backyard and sustainability focus make it especially appealing to design-conscious diners.
highlights: Michelin-starred, sustainability-minded tasting menu in an elegant Pangrati house with a garden courtyard.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; This is Athens; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Makris Athens brings a highly visual Greek tasting menu to a historic building opposite the Ancient Agora. Chef Petros Dimas works with produce from his own farm and frames the meal around heritage, zero-waste thinking and precise modern technique. The glass floors, ancient remains and Acropolis-adjacent terrace give the restaurant a strong sense of place.
highlights: New Michelin-starred Greek tasting menu, own-farm produce, ancient Agora setting and dramatic archaeological interiors.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Pelagos is the fine-dining flagship of the Four Seasons Astir Palace, giving Athens a polished Riviera seafood destination. The cooking is refined, Mediterranean and product-driven, with the resort setting raising the occasion. It is one of the clearest choices for luxury travelers staying on the coast but still dining within the Athens market.
highlights: Michelin-starred seafood-focused fine dining at Four Seasons Astir Palace with Athenian Riviera glamour.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; This is Athens; Travel.gr; Official website
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens

description: CTC is a confident contemporary Greek tasting-menu restaurant in Kerameikos, built around surprise, seasonality and refined technique. Chef Alexandros Tsiotinis uses a blind menu structure to make the dinner feel theatrical without losing polish. The neoclassical courtyard setting adds warmth to one of the city's most serious modern kitchens.
highlights: Michelin-starred blind tasting menu, modern Greek technique and atmospheric Kerameikos courtyard.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Time Out; Official website

description: Tudor Hall is a grand hotel fine-dining room above Syntagma Square, with old-world formality and a privileged Acropolis view. The menu modernizes Greek flavors while keeping the service and room firmly in luxury-hotel territory. It is a natural business, anniversary or first-night-in-Athens choice for affluent guests.
highlights: Michelin-starred rooftop fine dining at King George with Acropolis views and grand hotel service.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website
hotel_name_hint: King George, a Luxury Collection Hotel

description: Botrini's is the Halandri fine-dining restaurant of Ettore Botrini, bringing Greco-Italian personality to modern Mediterranean tasting menus. The restaurant is more residential than central, but its culinary reputation makes the short trip feel justified. It remains one of the strongest Athens choices for diners who want Michelin technique without a hotel setting.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern Mediterranean restaurant with Greco-Italian roots and a suburban destination feel.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Hytra has long been a benchmark for modern Greek fine dining in Athens. Its tasting menus translate local ingredients through a contemporary lens, while the room and service keep the experience polished. The restaurant's move to Ilisia preserves its role as one of the city's major chef-driven destinations.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern Greek tasting menus with rooftop heritage and a polished contemporary identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Patio is The Margi's intimate fine-dining restaurant in Vouliagmeni, shaped around seasonal produce and a garden-to-table sensibility. The meal is polished and quietly luxurious rather than flashy, matching the hotel's understated Riviera mood. It is especially relevant for guests splitting time between central Athens and the coast.
highlights: Michelin-starred resort fine dining at The Margi with seasonal menus and a sustainability-led garden philosophy.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Herve is a compact chef's-table restaurant in Petralona, built around close-up cooking, precision and an immersive evening rhythm. The format is intimate and contemporary, making it feel more like a culinary performance than a conventional dining room. It suits diners who prefer focused creativity over grand hotel glamour.
highlights: Michelin-starred chef's-table experience with an intimate, immersive format in Petralona.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: The Zillers gives Athens a compact Michelin-starred rooftop experience in the historic center. The cooking is contemporary Greek-Mediterranean, but the real strength is the combination of precision, intimacy and a direct Acropolis-facing setting. It is one of the city's most useful fine-dining choices for travelers staying around Plaka and Syntagma.
highlights: Michelin-starred rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views, historic-center convenience and polished modern Greek cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; This is Athens; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Varoulko Seaside remains one of the great names of modern Greek seafood, even though it no longer carries a current Michelin star. Lefteris Lazarou's Piraeus waterfront restaurant pairs refined fish cooking with a direct view of Mikrolimano's harbor. For luxury travelers who want a formal seafood dinner outside the center, it is still an essential Athens address.
highlights: Historic modern Greek seafood institution with Mikrolimano harbor views, tasting menus and strong wine service.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Athinorama; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Matsuhisa Athens brings the Nobu-Matsuhisa universe to the Athenian Riviera. The restaurant's Japanese-Peruvian signatures, resort setting and international clientele make it a natural affluent social-dining choice. It is not the city's most local table, but it is one of its most reliable luxury alternatives to formal fine dining.
highlights: Nobu-style Japanese-Peruvian dining at Astir Palace with Riviera views, black cod, robata and a polished international crowd.
sources: FNL Guide; Conde Nast Traveler; Travel.gr; Official website
hotel_name_hint: Four Seasons Astir Palace Hotel Athens

description: Aleria is a mature modern Greek restaurant in Metaxourgeio, set in a renovated neoclassical house with a garden. Chef Gikas Xenakis's tasting menus are elegant, Mediterranean and rooted in Greek memory rather than trend. It remains one of the city's strongest non-Michelin fine-dining alternatives.
highlights: Modern Greek tasting menus in a neoclassical mansion with a romantic garden and polished service.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Cookoovaya is one of Athens' defining modern Greek restaurants, balancing serious sourcing with a lively, grown-up dining room. The cooking is generous and ingredient-led rather than precious, with the Greek pantry treated through a contemporary lens. It works especially well for affluent diners who want atmosphere and quality without a tasting-menu commitment.
highlights: Contemporary Greek cooking, premium produce, lively Ilisia setting and a reputation as a serious local dining room.
sources: FNL Guide; Michelin Guide; Eater; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Papaioannou is one of the benchmark Greek fish restaurants in the Athens area, now operating in a polished coastal setting at Kavouri. The appeal is whole fish, shellfish, raw seafood, direct cooking and a wine list built around the sea. It is a classic Athenian seafood splurge for diners who prefer product purity to theatrics.
highlights: Top-tier Greek seafood, coastal Kavouri setting, whole fish, shellfish and a mature affluent crowd.
sources: FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: GB Roof Garden is the Grande Bretagne's signature rooftop restaurant, combining Mediterranean cooking with one of the most privileged views in central Athens. The room is grand, polished and useful for business, celebration or a first luxury dinner in the city. Its wine program and service make it more than just a view restaurant.
highlights: Grand hotel rooftop dining with Acropolis, Lycabettus and Parliament views, Mediterranean menu and Wine Spectator-recognized wine program.
sources: Michelin Guide; Marriott; FNL Guide; Official website
hotel_name_hint: Hotel Grande Bretagne, a Luxury Collection Hotel

description: Dolli's Rooftop Restaurant is one of Athens' most glamorous new luxury-hotel dining rooms, with an unusually direct Parthenon view. The cooking is refined and cosmopolitan, matching the art-filled boutique-hotel mood below. It is strongest as a stylish, high-touch dinner for travelers who care as much about setting as plate work.
highlights: Ravishing rooftop restaurant at The Dolli with Parthenon views, polished service and a fashionably affluent crowd.
sources: Michelin Guide; Travel.gr; The Dolli; Official website

description: SENSE is the rooftop restaurant of AthensWas, pairing modern Greek cuisine with a close Acropolis backdrop. The style is polished and aesthetic, with degustation options and a strong sense of occasion at sunset. It is a useful luxury-dining choice for guests based around the Acropolis Museum and Makrygianni.
highlights: Elegant rooftop at AthensWas with modern Greek cuisine, Acropolis views and dinner-only special-occasion appeal.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; This is Athens; Official website

description: Simul is a polished Kolonaki bistronomic restaurant with a playful, flavor-led approach to Greek ingredients. The dining room is intimate, chic and relaxed, making it a strong alternative to formal tasting menus. It fits the affluent-diner brief because the cooking is serious, the service is knowledgeable and the mood is confidently contemporary.
highlights: Creative bistronomic plates, polished Kolonaki mood, tasting-menu option and expert wine pairing.
sources: Michelin Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Iodio is a refined Kolonaki seafood restaurant with a contemporary Greek-Mediterranean point of view. The kitchen treats fish, shellfish and bottarga with creative precision, while the room keeps a serene, grown-up mood. It is one of the city's strongest newer choices for upscale seafood away from the waterfront.
highlights: Contemporary seafood in Kolonaki with minimalist design, creative fish dishes and a relaxed luxury feel.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Gallina is a Koukaki modern bistro that has quickly become part of Athens' serious dining conversation. The cooking is precise and contemporary, but the room stays social and approachable rather than ceremonial. It is a good choice for an affluent traveler looking for a current, design-aware Athens dinner outside the Michelin-star circuit.
highlights: Modern Koukaki bistro with polished cooking, confident service and contemporary local energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: see|ds is a modern Athens restaurant with an open-kitchen spirit and a quiet luxury aesthetic. The menu is chef-driven, seasonal and flexible enough to support a custom tasting experience, while the private loft and wine-cellar elements add grown-up appeal. It is a strong under-the-radar choice for diners who want refinement without the formality of a star.
highlights: Michelin-selected modern restaurant with open kitchen, private loft, wine-cellar table and custom tasting-menu potential.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Akra is a current Pangrati favorite from a strong chef team, mixing bakery energy, open-fire cooking and a daily-changing Greek menu. It is more relaxed than a classic fine-dining room, but the sourcing, technique and buzz make it highly relevant to sophisticated diners. The restaurant captures Athens' new confidence in informal but serious cooking.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand, daily-changing Greek menu, open fire, chef pedigree and intimate Pangrati room.
sources: Michelin Guide; Travel.gr; Official Instagram

description: Pharaoh is a wood-fire, wine-led Greek restaurant in Exarchia that feels both deeply local and extremely current. The room combines natural wines, vinyl and an industrial mood with cooking rooted in older Greek flavors. It is one of Athens' most convincing examples of relaxed dining that still matters to affluent, well-traveled guests.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand, wood-fire Greek cooking, natural wine, vinyl and a modern-industrial Exarchia atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; FNL Guide; Travel.gr; 50 Best Discovery; Official website

description: Esthio brings Balkan-Greek cooking into a refined Koukaki setting near the Acropolis. Chef Elvi-Dimitris Zyba reworks family recipes and regional flavors with a more polished, contemporary hand. It gives Athens' luxury dining map a distinctive voice beyond the usual modern Greek and seafood categories.
highlights: Michelin-listed Balkan-Greek restaurant in a 1931 neoclassical building close to the Acropolis.
sources: Michelin Guide; Travel.gr; Official website

description: Vezene is a polished Greek bistro and grill with a wood-fired kitchen, regional products and a serious meat-and-seafood following. It has the feel of a confident neighborhood restaurant that also attracts visitors, business diners and regulars with high standards. The atmosphere is less formal than fine dining, but the sourcing and execution place it firmly in Athens' affluent dinner set.
highlights: Wood-fired Greek bistro with sustainable meat, local seafood, regional dishes and a lively grown-up room.
sources: FNL Guide; Travel.gr; Eater; Official website

description: Nyn Esti places modern Greek dining inside the National Museum of Contemporary Art, giving the restaurant an unusually cultural frame. The room offers stylish hospitality and Acropolis views, while the kitchen is built for a composed dinner rather than a casual museum stop. It is one of Athens' more interesting design-conscious luxury alternatives.
highlights: Modern Greek restaurant at EMST with Acropolis views, museum setting and polished contemporary service.
sources: Time Out; Nyn Esti; EMST; InfoTouch; Official website

description: Papadakis is an elegant Kolonaki seafood classic from chef Argiro Barbarigou, rooted in Aegean island cooking. The restaurant is polished, central and especially strong for fish, seafood and Greek flavors in a quieter luxury neighborhood setting. It works well for diners who want an adult seafood dinner without traveling to the coast.
highlights: Kolonaki seafood institution with Aegean island cooking, fresh fish, celebrity-chef heritage and city-center convenience.
sources: This is Athens; Papadakis; Attica Gastronomy; Official website

description: Oikonomou is a historic Ano Petralona taverna with the kind of old-Athens rhythm that sophisticated diners often hope to find. The cooking is traditional, hearty and home-style, built around long-running regulars rather than design trends. It is included as a culturally meaningful relaxed dinner, not as a fine-dining substitute.
highlights: Historic 1930 Ano Petralona taverna with classic Greek home cooking and a strong neighborhood identity.
sources: Greek Gastronomy Guide; FNL Guide; Athens By Bike; Official website

description: Ama Lachei is a beloved Exarchia meze restaurant with a leafy courtyard and a relaxed all-evening rhythm. The food is built for sharing, with modern Greek touches layered onto familiar taverna culture. It is a strong local favorite for a lower-key night that still feels distinctly Athenian.
highlights: Exarchia courtyard mezedopoleio with shared Greek plates, friendly service and a lively local following.
sources: This is Athens; Restaurant Guru; Tripadvisor; Local dining guides

description: Seychelles is a modern Kerameikos taverna that helped define the neighborhood's contemporary Greek dining identity. The cooking is rustic, produce-focused and more ambitious than a basic tavern, while the pavement tables keep the evening relaxed. It belongs in the local-favorite layer because it gives visitors a real Athens meal with energy and substance.
highlights: Kerameikos modern taverna with rustic Greek dishes, small-producer ingredients and a strong local reputation.
sources: Greece Is; Seychelles; Local dining guides; Tripadvisor

description: Klimataria is one of central Athens' atmospheric old tavernas, close to the market and historic triangle. The appeal is traditional Greek food, wine, music and a room that feels embedded in the city's popular dining culture. It is not polished luxury, but it is exactly the kind of textured local dinner an experienced traveler can appreciate.
highlights: Seventy-year-plus historic taverna with traditional Greek dishes, house wine, live music and old-Athens atmosphere.
sources: Greece Is; Travel.gr; Klimataria; Restaurant Guru; Official website

description: Mavros Gatos is a genuine Pangrati neighborhood taverna with roots stretching back to 1963. The restaurant is known for quality meats, home-style dishes, Greek cheeses and a better-than-expected wine list for the category. It rounds out the Athens list as a relaxed, authentic local classic with enough culinary care for well-traveled diners.
highlights: Pangrati taverna operating since 1963, known for charcoal-grilled meats, home cooking, Greek cheeses and a warm neighborhood feel.
sources: Greece Is; Gastronomos; Local dining guides; Tripadvisor
